look_here_first: START WITH THE GREEN FLOWERING TIPS, THEN CHECK FRUIT. Warty spurge (E. spathulata) is a small hairless annual with alternate, spoon-shaped stem leaves and repeatedly forked upper branches. The broad leaflike bracts at the cyathia stay DISTINCT instead of making the strongly fused green cup of E. roemeriana. Under a hand lens, the green 3-lobed capsule has LOW ROUNDED WARTS; the tiny cyathial nectar glands have NO HORNS. Do not claim those microscopic features from the current hand-held whole-tip photo—it shows green flowering-bract clusters, not diagnostic capsule surface or seed sculpture.

morphology_keys.family_pattern: Euphorbiaceae; upright leafy Euphorbia subgenus Esula with tiny cyathia (specialized flowering units) rather than ordinary petals.
morphology_keys.habit: Hairless annual with slender upright, often basally branched shoots and repeatedly forked terminal reproductive branches.
morphology_keys.leaves: Stem leaves alternate and typically spatulate to oblanceolate, usually with finely serrulate margins; inspect several mature leaves rather than only bracts.
morphology_keys.paired_bracts: Paired upper dichasial bracts separate (distinct), often broadly ovate or triangular, sometimes with fine-toothed edges; not half-fused as in E. roemeriana.
morphology_keys.cyathia: Small green cup-like flowering units; 4–5 nectar glands without horns, requiring strong close-up to verify.
morphology_keys.fruit: Mature capsule shallowly 3-lobed and covered with small LOW ROUNDED verrucae (warts), a key difference from the smooth capsules of E. roemeriana.
morphology_keys.seed: Variable brown to dark-purple seeds; smooth, finely ridged or netlike-reticulate surfaces across geographic populations. Do not impose a universal reticulate seed texture on Texas specimens.
morphology_keys.source_note: Flora of North America, Euphorbia spathulata Lam. (taxon_id=242416545). Native-by-county review is paused; FNA is used for anatomy, not a finished Hays BONAP/NAPA badge.

comparisons.caution: An apparently cup-shaped green whorl is not proof of bract fusion: isolate one pair and inspect the basal seam. Do not use the one spathulata habit photo as proof of warty capsule or seed sculpture.

field_photo_quickcheck.heading: FIND THE FRUIT WARTS
steps: Photograph complete rooted plant, then stem leaves and margin teeth in focus.
Get close enough to isolate one pair of green dichasial bracts: confirm they are separate instead of fused halfway.
Photograph several fully developed green capsules at 10× or higher; look for small low rounded warts covering lobes.
Take a high-magnification cyathium view to confirm gland horns absent (do not substitute yellow color alone).
Optional: photograph a mature loose seed from two angles with 1mm scale; Texas seed texture may be smooth or reticulate.
field_photo_quickcheck.warning: Current sole photograph does not resolve gland horns, diagnostic warty capsules or seeds. Keep this one-photo species provisional for field diagnosis pending those photos.

diagnostic_image_needs.requirements: Exact species; sharp lateral and front views showing low rounded capsule verrucae; copyright compatible with educational website
Clear bases of two bracts and visible serrulate margin where present
10–30× focused cyathium cup showing glands without horns
Whole rooted herb and leaf margins free of unrelated foreground plants
Exact Texas taxon source; seed coat close-up with millimeter scale if available
